subject: Coaching plan and next steps for Evelyn - pre-PIP documentation
messages:

To: monica.patel@redwood.example.com, markus.klein@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft coaching plan for Evelyn (pre-PIP)

Monica / Markus,

Quick context: Evelyn's throughput and hit-rate on SRE oncall tickets has declined over the last three quarters and she's missed two OKR milestones this quarter. I've been doing 1:1s and gave specific feedback in early January and again in mid-February, but progress is limited. I'm looking to document a short, time-boxed coaching plan (4 weeks) to set clear expectations and provide supports before any formal PIP.

Attached is my draft coaching plan (confidential). I want HR's view on language, required timelines, and any compliance steps we should follow. Key asks:
- Is a 4-week coaching window appropriate vs 6 weeks?
- What documentation do we need to keep on file?
- Recommended phrasing to avoid triggering immediate PIP while preserving a clear escalation path.

Attachment: 20260225_draft-coaching-plan.docx

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: monica.patel@redwood.example.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft coaching plan for Evelyn (pre-PIP)

Laura,

Thanks for the note and for documenting the conversations so far. This is the right approach — we recommend a structured pre-PIP coaching plan (4–6 weeks depending on role) with explicit objectives, measurable success criteria, and a scheduled mid-point check-in. A few HR notes:

- Use the attached HR_prePIP_template_v2.pdf as the canonical document; it contains recommended wording for expectations and supports.
- Keep all 1:1 notes and meeting invites in one shared folder (link below).
- Make sure the employee receives the plan in writing and has at least 48 hours to ask clarifying questions before the first checkpoint.
- If the employee requests reasonable accommodations, pause timelines and escalate to People Ops.

On your specific questions: 4 weeks is acceptable for a focused operational role like Evelyn's if the objectives are measurable (e.g., ticket resolution SLA, number of successful handoffs, runbook updates). For documentation, retain the plan, meeting notes, and any performance data for 2 years per our retention policy.

I've attached the HR template and added a sample phrasing block below you can use when you share the plan with Evelyn.

Sample phrasing (you can adapt):
"This coaching plan is intended to give you focused support on specific performance areas. Over the next four weeks we will set measurable goals and review progress at the two-week mark. The goal of this plan is to support your success; if progress remains insufficient we will discuss next steps, which may include formal performance processes."

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExampleCoachingFolder

Attachment: HR_prePIP_template_v2.pdf

Best,
Monica Patel
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.example.com
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.example.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Coaching plan: focused support and 4-week expectations

Evelyn,

Following our 1:1s and the conversations we've had over the past two months, I've put together a focused 4-week coaching plan to help you get back on track with team expectations. Monica from People Ops is cc'd for visibility. This is a supportive step meant to clarify expectations and provide resources — it is not a formal PIP today, but it does set clear outcomes and timelines.

Please find the plan attached (Evelyn_Performance_Coaching_2026-03-02.pdf). Highlights:
- Timebox: 4 weeks (Mar 3 — Mar 30)
- Objectives (examples):
  * Reduce oncall escalations attributable to handoff errors by 50%
  * Close tickets in the SRE backlog to meet team SLA (mean time to close target: 48 hours)
  * Complete two prioritized runbook updates and shadowing sessions
- Success criteria: explicit metrics per objective, reviewed at week 2 and week 4
- Supports offered: dedicated pairing sessions (2x/week), access to training budget for the observability stack, flexible schedule for overlap with senior oncall
- Consequence ladder: if objectives are not met after this coaching window we will move to a formal performance process (we will review options with People Ops first).

Please review and let me know any clarifying questions by end-of-day Thursday. We'll schedule a kickoff meeting for Wed 3/4 at 3pm and the week-2 checkpoint for Mon 3/16 at 10am.

Attachment: Evelyn_Performance_Coaching_2026-03-02.pdf

Thanks for taking the time to go through this. I want to ensure you have everything you need to succeed — if you need more support with pacing or resources let me know.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: evelyn.hart@redwood.example.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.example.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coaching plan: focused support and 4-week expectations

Hi Laura,

Thanks for sending this. I appreciate the clarity and the pairing sessions. A couple of quick clarifying questions before the kickoff:

1) For the ticket closure metric, can we confirm whether the 48-hour target is business days or calendar hours? I want to ensure measurement is fair given weekends.
2) For the shadowing sessions, are these mandatory or optional? I may need to shift some non-critical tasks to attend.
3) If training is needed beyond the small course you suggested, what is the approval path and expected lead time?

I plan to review the attached doc and will bring any additional questions to the kickoff. I want to do well here and appreciate the offer to pair.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.example.com
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.example.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coaching plan: focused support and 4-week expectations

Evelyn — thanks for the quick questions and for engaging. Short answers below and I'll also update the doc before the kickoff: 

1) The 48-hour SLA is calendar hours for ticket triage/acknowledgement, but measurement excludes weekends/holidays — I'll add that note to the plan.
2) Shadowing sessions are strongly recommended and counted toward your success criteria; if there is an unavoidable conflict please propose alternate slots and we'll work with you.
3) If the training suggested in the plan is insufficient, escalate to me and Monica. For more substantial courses we'll need People Ops approval (we'll aim for a 7–10 business day approval window).

Kickoff still stands for Thu 3/12 at 3pm (calendar invite sent). If anything changes, ping me.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Engineering
